The image shows a chromium(2+) ion and two cyclopentadienyl anions, each drawn as a five-membered ring with two C=C double bonds and a CH⁻ vertex.

Each ring has five carbons: the CH⁻ carbon, two carbons joined by one double bond, and two more joined by the second double bond. As SMILES, one anion is [CH-]1C=CC=C1.

The chromium is written as [Cr+2]. The three species are separate, so I join them with dots.

SMILES: [Cr+2].[CH-]1C=CC=C1.[CH-]1C=CC=C1
